item.title: Nara Fude: The Calligraphy Brushes of the Ancient Capital — Guide
item.description: Nara fude (calligraphy brushes) are among Japan’s most esteemed, a craft that arrived with Buddhism and brush-writing in the 8th century and has been refined in the old capital ever since. Making a fine brush is exacting handwork: hairs from goats, horses, weasels and other animals are sorted, cleaned, blended in precise proportions and bundled by hand into a tip that holds ink perfectly and springs back with just the right resilience — qualities calligraphers prize above all.

item.title: Joboji Urushi Lacquer: Japan's Lacquer Heartland — Iwate Guide
item.description: Joboji, in Ninohe in northern Iwate, produces the majority of Japan’s precious domestic urushi (natural lacquer) — the sap tapped from lacquer trees that coats the finest traditional crafts and restores national treasures. In this craft town you can try lacquer-coating or maki-e (gold-relief) decoration of a bowl, a hands-on encounter with a rare Japanese art. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Ninohe (Joboji), Iwate Hours By reservation Admission Workshop ~¥3,000 Time needed About 1.

item.title: Kogin-zashi Embroidery: Tsugaru's Geometric Stitch — Guide
item.description: Kogin-zashi is Tsugaru’s centuries-old counted-thread embroidery — crisp white geometric patterns stitched onto indigo cloth, originally to reinforce and warm farmers' work clothes. Hirosaki workshops let you stitch a small coaster or accessory, a calming, hands-on encounter with a beautiful folk craft. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hirosaki, Aomori Hours By reservation Admission Workshop ~¥2,000 Time needed About 1.

item.title: Nanbu Ironware (Tetsubin): Morioka's 400-Year Craft — Guide
item.description: Nanbu tekki (southern Iwate ironware) is one of Japan’s most celebrated crafts — hand-cast iron teapots (tetsubin) and cookware made in Morioka and Mizusawa for over 400 years, with distinctive pebbled surfaces. Several Morioka workshops offer casting experiences and studio tours; the finished pieces are used for a lifetime and handed down through generations. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Morioka, Iwate Hours Workshop/shop hours Admission Casting workshop ~¥3,500–4,000 Time needed 1–2 hours Best time Year-round What to Do Watch or try casting iron at a Morioka atelier.

item.title: Tendo Shogi: 95% of Japan's Chess Pieces & Human Shogi — Guide
item.description: Tendo produces over 95% of all shogi (Japanese chess) pieces in Japan, and the town’s artisans hand-carve and ink the characters onto boxwood pieces using techniques unchanged for 150 years. The Tendo Shogi Museum and craft workshops welcome visitors, and each spring the city hosts the famous ‘Ningen Shogi’ (Human Shogi) tournament, where people in Sengoku costume play as the living pieces on a giant outdoor board atop Maizuru Park.

item.title: Tsugaru Vidro Glass: Blow Your Own in Aomori — Guide
item.description: Tsugaru Vidro (biidoro) is Aomori’s vivid handmade glass, its jewel colours echoing the region’s seas, forests and four seasons. Studios near Aomori City let you try glass-blowing to shape your own tumbler or ornament — a warm, memorable hands-on souvenir of your trip. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City area Hours By reservation Admission Experience ~¥3,000 Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round What to Expect Blow your own glass tumbler or ornament.

item.title: Tsugaru-nuri Lacquerware: Aomori's Jewel-Like Craft — Guide
item.description: Tsugaru-nuri is Aomori’s signature lacquerware, famed for its mottled, jewel-like patterns built up from dozens of painstaking layers of coloured lacquer. At Hirosaki workshops you can try the final polishing step that reveals the hidden pattern — a hands-on window into a 300-year craft tradition. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hirosaki, Aomori Hours By reservation Admission Workshop ~¥2,500 Time needed About 1.

item.title: Aomori Girls' Trip: Hirosaki Sweets, Apple Farm Retreats & Onsen Weekends
item.description: Aomori Girls' Group Travel Guide: Apples, Art & Adventure in Northern Japan Aomori Prefecture, Japan’s northernmost region on Honshu island, offers the perfect blend of sweet indulgences, cultural experiences, and Instagram-worthy moments for an unforgettable girls' trip. From apple-themed everything to festival dancing and peaceful onsen retreats, here’s your complete guide to exploring this underrated destination with your best friends. 1. Hirosaki’s Sweet Paradise: Apple Pie Trail & Patisserie Culture Welcome to Japan’s apple capital!

item.title: Toyama Leisure Guide: Kurobe Dam, Alpine Route Crossing, Inami Woodcarving & Tonami Tulips
item.description: Toyama’s leisure options split between large-scale engineering spectacle and intimate craft tradition. A single trip can move from standing at the base of a 186-metre dam arch to sitting in a woodcarver’s workshop in a quiet temple town — and both experiences feel genuinely specific to this prefecture. Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route: Full Crossing The Alpine Route crossing is one of Japan’s great leisure journeys, best approached as a full-day experience rather than a rushed transit.

item.title: Yamagata Girls' Trip: Ginzan Onsen Retreat, Cherry Picking & Sake Tasting
item.description: Girls' Group Travel Guide to Yamagata Prefecture Yamagata Prefecture offers the perfect blend of romantic onsen towns, seasonal fruit adventures, sake culture, and vibrant festivals—ideal for an unforgettable girls' trip to Japan’s Tohoku region. 1. Ginzan Onsen: The Ultimate Girls' Retreat Ginzan Onsen looks like it stepped out of a Studio Ghibli film, with its lantern-lit street along a mountain stream and historic wooden ryokan. For groups, planning an overnight stay requires strategic booking, but the experience of wandering through this magical town together in matching yukata is absolutely worth it.

item.title: Fukui Girls' Trip: Eyeglass Frame Shopping, Onsen Hopping & Coastal Cafés
item.description: Fukui Prefecture is not where most girls' trips are planned, and that is a missed opportunity of considerable scale. A prefecture that produces 95% of Japan’s eyeglass frames, runs some of the country’s most elegant ryokan, offers hands-on craft workshops in one of Japan’s most historic paper-making towns, and delivers dramatic coastal scenery for exactly the kind of photographs that actually do the experience justice — this is a destination worth building an itinerary around.
